successCriteria.description: AuditService no longer imports or references `Pool` from `pg` — it depends on `IAuditRepository` via constructor injection, and all database access is delegated to the repository.
An `IAuditRepository` interface exists with an `insert` method that accepts `Omit<AuditRecord, 'id' | 'createdAt'>` and an optional `PoolClient`, returning `Promise<AuditRecord>`.

An `AuditRepository` class implements `IAuditRepository`, using the shared `pool` from `src/shared/db/connection.ts` for its default connection and accepting an optional `PoolClient` for transactional use.
The audit module barrel export (`src/modules/audit/index.ts`) exports `IAuditRepository` and `AuditRepository` alongside the existing `AuditRecord`, `IAuditService`, and `AuditService`.
The existing `IAuditService.record` contract is unchanged — consumers of `IAuditService` (including `LeaveRequestService` in Phase 4) require zero changes to their code.

The existing audit service unit test (`tests/unit/modules/audit/audit.service.test.ts`) is updated to mock `IAuditRepository` instead of `Pool`, and a new unit test for `AuditRepository` exists at `tests/unit/modules/audit/audit.repository.test.ts`.

constraints: The `no-direct-db-outside-repository` constraint (HARNESS.json, severity: critical) must be satisfied — after this phase, no service in the audit module may call `pool.query()` or import `Pool` from `pg`.

The `IAuditRepository.insert` method must accept an optional `client: PoolClient` parameter to support the transaction contract defined in `.gestalt/architecture/reconciled.json` — when provided, the method uses it for the query and does NOT release it; when omitted, it acquires from the shared pool internally.
The `AuditService` constructor must accept `IAuditRepository` (not `Pool`), matching the pattern established by `EmployeeService` which accepts `IEmployeeRepository`.
outOfScope: Adding query methods to `IAuditRepository` beyond `insert` (e.g., `findByEntity`, `findByDateRange`). Only the `insert` method is needed to replace the current direct-DB access in `AuditService.record`.

entityInvariants.invariant: Every `AuditRecord` inserted must have `id` generated by the database (via `gen_random_uuid()`) and `createdAt` set to the insertion timestamp — the caller provides only `entityType`, `entityId`, `action`, `performedBy`, and `changes`.

interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Must throw if the database insert fails (connection error, constraint violation). The caller is responsible for wrapping in a transaction when atomicity with other operations is required.
Delegates to IAuditRepository.insert. The contract signature and return type are unchanged from the current implementation — existing consumers are unaffected.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: The `IAuditRepository` interface and `AuditRepository` implementation must follow the same pattern as `IEmployeeRepository` / `EmployeeRepository`: the interface declares the contract, the implementation imports the shared `pool` from `src/shared/db/connection.ts`, and the optional `client: PoolClient` parameter enables transactional use.

The `AuditService.record` method must produce the same SQL insert (`INSERT INTO audit_records ... RETURNING ...`) and the same column-to-property mapping (`entity_type AS "entityType"`, `entity_id AS "entityId"`, `performed_by AS "performedBy"`, `created_at AS "createdAt"`) that currently exists in `src/modules/audit/audit.service.ts` line 9-13 — the SQL moves to the repository but the query semantics must not change.

integrationPoints.why: LeaveRequestService depends on IAuditService.record for GP-002 audit trail on every state transition. The IAuditService interface is unchanged by this phase, so no consumer code changes are required.
AuditRepository imports the shared `pool` singleton, same as EmployeeRepository. No change to the connection module.
